answer: Here is one mechanism that works: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because nebula only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, umber is enforced in the ledger: Jurors see the identity's full answer chain, so a template match is detectable in one pass. Any opal approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
